solution_overview:
A retailer analyzed loyalty card ownership among its customers. One customer is selected at random. Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be the events that the customer holds Card X, Card Y, and Card Z, respectively. The given probabilities are:

$P(X) = 0.52$
$P(Y) = 0.34$
$P(Z) = 0.41$

$P(X \cap Y) = 0.18$
$P(X \cap Z) = 0.22$
$P(Y \cap Z) = 0.15$

$P(X \cap Y \cap Z) = 0.09$

We can decompose the sample space into mutually exclusive regions representing customers holding exactly 0, 1, 2, or 3 cards. Let $P(E_k)$ denote the probability that a customer holds exactly $k$ cards.

The probability of holding all three cards is directly given:
$$P(E_3) = P(X \cap Y \cap Z) = 0.09$$

The probabilities of holding exactly two specific cards (e.g., only X and Y, but not Z) are calculated by subtracting the probability of holding all three cards from the pairwise intersection probabilities:
$$P(X \cap Y \cap Z^c) = P(X \cap Y) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z)$$
$$P(X \cap Y \cap Z^c) = 0.18 - 0.09 = 0.09$$
$$P(X \cap Z \cap Y^c) = P(X \cap Z) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z)$$
$$P(X \cap Z \cap Y^c) = 0.22 - 0.09 = 0.13$$
$$P(Y \cap Z \cap X^c) = P(Y \cap Z) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z)$$
$$P(Y \cap Z \cap X^c) = 0.15 - 0.09 = 0.06$$

The probability of holding exactly two cards, $P(E_2)$, is the sum of these three mutually exclusive probabilities:
$$P(E_2) = P(X \cap Y \cap Z^c) + P(X \cap Z \cap Y^c) + P(Y \cap Z \cap X^c)$$
$$P(E_2) = 0.09 + 0.13 + 0.06 = 0.28$$

The probabilities of holding exactly one specific card (e.g., only X, but not Y or Z) are found by subtracting all relevant two-card and three-card intersection probabilities from the single-card probability:
$$P(X \cap Y^c \cap Z^c) = P(X) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z^c) - P(X \cap Z \cap Y^c) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z)$$
$$P(X \cap Y^c \cap Z^c) = 0.52 - 0.09 - 0.13 - 0.09 = 0.21$$
$$P(Y \cap X^c \cap Z^c) = P(Y) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z^c) - P(Y \cap Z \cap X^c) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z)$$
$$P(Y \cap X^c \cap Z^c) = 0.34 - 0.09 - 0.06 - 0.09 = 0.10$$
$$P(Z \cap X^c \cap Y^c) = P(Z) - P(X \cap Z \cap Y^c) - P(Y \cap Z \cap X^c) - P(X \cap Y \cap Z)$$
$$P(Z \cap X^c \cap Y^c) = 0.41 - 0.13 - 0.06 - 0.09 = 0.13$$

The probability of holding exactly one card, $P(E_1)$, is the sum of these three mutually exclusive probabilities:
$$P(E_1) = P(X \cap Y^c \cap Z^c) + P(Y \cap X^c \cap Z^c) + P(Z \cap X^c \cap Y^c)$$
$$P(E_1) = 0.21 + 0.10 + 0.13 = 0.44$$

The total probability of holding at least one card is the sum of the probabilities of holding exactly one, two, or three cards:
$$P(X \cup Y \cup Z) = P(E_1) + P(E_2) + P(E_3)$$
$$P(X \cup Y \cup Z) = 0.44 + 0.28 + 0.09 = 0.81$$

Finally, the probability of holding none of the cards, $P(E_0)$, is the complement of holding at least one card:
$$P(E_0) = 1 - P(X \cup Y \cup Z)$$
$$P(E_0) = 1 - 0.81 = 0.19$$
These values $P(E_0)=0.19$, $P(E_1)=0.44$, $P(E_2)=0.28$, $P(E_3)=0.09$ summarize the distribution of card ownership.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The probability that a customer holds at least one card is the probability of the union of the three card-holding events, $X \cup Y \cup Z$. The Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion for three events computes this probability as:
$$P(X \cup Y \cup Z) = P(X) + P(Y) + P(Z) - (P(X \cap Y) + P(X \cap Z) + P(Y \cap Z)) + P(X \cap Y \cap Z)$$
Substitute the given probabilities into the formula:
$$P(X \cup Y \cup Z) = 0.52 + 0.34 + 0.41 - (0.18 + 0.22 + 0.15) + 0.09$$
$$P(X \cup Y \cup Z) = 1.27 - 0.55 + 0.09$$
$$P(X \cup Y \cup Z) = 0.72 + 0.09 = 0.81$$
This result is $0.81$, or $81\%$. Since $81\% > 79\%$, the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The probability that the customer holds exactly one card is $P(E_1)$. From the calculations in the solution overview, we have:
$$P(E_1) = 0.44$$
This value represents $44\%$. Since $44\% > 42\%$, the statement is True.

**C.** → True

The probability that the customer holds exactly two cards is $P(E_2)$. From the calculations in the solution overview, we have:
$$P(E_2) = 0.28$$
This value represents $28\%$. Since $28\% \ge 26\%$, the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The event "none of the three cards" is the complement of the event "at least one card." The probability of holding none of the cards is $P(E_0)$. From the calculations in the solution overview, we have:
$$P(E_0) = 0.19$$
This value represents $19\%$. Since $19\% < 21\%$, the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The probability that the customer holds at least two cards means the sum of the probabilities of holding exactly two cards, $P(E_2)$, and exactly three cards, $P(E_3)$. From the calculations in the solution overview, we have $P(E_2) = 0.28$ and $P(E_3) = 0.09$.
$$P(\text{at least two}) = P(E_2) + P(E_3)$$
$$P(\text{at least two}) = 0.28 + 0.09 = 0.37$$
This value represents $37\%$. Since $37\% > 35\%$, the statement is True.
